mitre_technique_note: ATT&CK describes attacker tradecraft; 'a feature marked deprecated was never actually removed from the running service' is a decommissioning-hygiene gap, not a technique. Same honest gap as pt05 and pt15.
cwe_note: No CWE maps this precisely; CWE-16 (Configuration) is the closest broad parent, same kind of imprecise-but-honest mapping pt15 uses CWE-840 for.
description: The B2B complaint-via-XML/YAML upload path is described by Juice Shop's own challenge catalog as 'a deprecated B2B interface that was not properly shut down.' A true decommissioning would make the route return 404, as if it never existed. Instead it returns HTTP 410 with a 'deprecated for security reasons' message, still executing real logic (file parsing) before saying so, exactly the half-measure pt17 was able to exploit for XXE. Decommissioning on paper is not decommissioning in the running service.
expected_exploit_indicator: An uploaded .xml or .yml file gets a deliberate, logic-executing response (HTTP 410) rather than a plain 404, proving the route is still live
legitimate_check: A .pdf complaint attachment, the actual still-supported path, must keep getting its normal HTTP 204 response.
